summary: T-0658 [security/системный, столп 4]: getGrantsForSubject (src/db/grants-dao.ts:208) is the single canonical grant resolver every PDP consumer uses (invoke.ts, records.ts field/read-visibility, org.ts capability-token, sandbox-gate-dao.ts, capability-grants-dao.ts, registry-digest-dao.ts). Its step 1 resolved subject slug -> employee id with NO `deactivated_at IS NULL` predicate. A deactivated (fired) employee (T-0583/migration 125: KC login disabled, deactivated_at set) whose already-issued KC access token is still within its own TTL (KC enabled:false blocks only future token issuance, not an already-issued token — a window of minutes) still resolved to an employee row here, so every downstream PDP consumer of this resolver granted them their normal privileges. inbox.ts had already grown its OWN local `deactivatedAt != null` gate (T-0588 BLOCK-3 claim / RE-VERIFY approve) precisely because of this upstream gap — an asymmetric per-path defence that every current and future consumer would otherwise have to remember to duplicate. Fix: added `AND deactivated_at IS NULL` to step 1's SQL (fail-closed) — a deactivated subject now resolves to zero employee rows, so getGrantsForSubject returns [] for them, symmetric with the pre-existing 'unknown actor' sentinel. This closes the gap once, for every consumer, instead of per-path. Human vs agent: this is ONE query against choros.employee with no branch on kind — both human and agent subjects resolve through the same step 1 (register.ts:364 confirms there is no separate agent resolution path). deactivated_at (migration 125) is a column on employee shared by both kinds, but its ONLY write site (PATCH /api/users/:employee_id, user-mgmt.ts:522) is structurally restricted to kind==='human' (404 otherwise) — agent_card (migration 032) carries no deactivation column of its own, so a kind='agent' row's deactivated_at is always NULL in production. The unconditional predicate is therefore a permanent no-op for legitimate agents and a real fail-closed gate for humans, with no kind-branch needed for correctness. Ripple analysis (ADR §3) over every consumer of getGrantsForSubject found none relying on a deactivated subject resolving to a non-empty grant set (e.g. no admin/audit path reads terminated-employee grants through this resolver) — the fix is a pure narrowing.

AC-3 — positive control: the identical grant/assignment shape on an ACTIVE employee (deactivated_at NULL) still resolves the grant normally (happy path unaffected). AC-4 — a kind='agent' employee with the identical grant shape resolves the grant normally too (agent resolution structurally untouched by the new predicate, since agent rows never carry a non-NULL deactivated_at). live_proof_plan: Security-debt fix on an internal PDP authority-resolution function (getGrantsForSubject is not user-facing UI) — the strongest available proof is the live-Postgres db test exercising the REAL SQL every consumer depends on, seeded with the exact failure shape (a deactivated employee with an otherwise fully PDP-active, dual-confirmed critical grant) and proving both directions: the gap closes (AC-2) and the happy path survives (AC-3/AC-4). A founder-facing click-through does not add proof here beyond what T-0588's inbox.ts claim/approve LIVE_PROOF already demonstrated for the symptom-level gate; this task closes the same class of hole at its source so every OTHER PDP surface (invoke, records read/write, org capability-token, sandbox-gate) gets the same guarantee without a dedicated screen to click per surface.
fix: src/db/grants-dao.ts, getGrantsForSubject step 1: SQL changed from `SELECT id FROM choros.employee WHERE tenant_id = $1 AND slug = $2 LIMIT 1` to `SELECT id FROM choros.employee WHERE tenant_id = $1 AND slug = $2 AND deactivated_at IS NULL LIMIT 1`. Single additive AND clause, no new parameter, no branch on kind. Extended the surrounding comment (recon findings: why this predicate is safe for agents, cross-reference to the other deactivation-aware readers in the same file, cross-reference to inbox.ts's now-redundant local gates) and the 'unknown actor' fallback comment (now covers 'unknown OR deactivated'). Steps 2 (role_assignment) and 3 (grant, dual-control) are byte-unchanged.

findings_out_of_scope: inbox.ts's own local deactivation gates (T-0588 BLOCK-3 claim ~line 1413-1417, RE-VERIFY approve ~line 1631-1643) are now redundant defence-in-depth rather than the sole line of defence — left in place per the task's additive-only instruction (removing them is a separate simplification follow-up, not required to close the security gap; ADR §7/spec §7 record this explicitly as out-of-scope).

This fix closes the PDP-resolution gap inside Choros only. It does NOT shorten or revoke the underlying live KC access token itself — the window between deactivation and that token's own TTL expiry still exists at the authentication layer (a deactivated user can still present a still-valid token and pass AUTHENTICATION; this fix ensures every AUTHORIZATION decision through getGrantsForSubject now correctly returns no grants for them in that window). Shortening that window (e.g. KC session/token revocation on deactivation) is a separate, larger task noted in spec §7 as out-of-scope for T-0658.
